scenario: A same-conversation synthetic coding escalation: diagnose the failing Python test, then respond to the terse follow-up “Fix it.”

method.hermes: 0.21.5 clean source for both arms; HADES arm loads current sitecustomize overlay
method.reasoning: disabled; max output 512 tokens per generation
method.runtime: same isolated rootless Docker daemon and immutable sandbox image; containers network=none
method.subject: synthetic owner identity; private fixture only
method.workspace: Private synthetic Git repository, initially failing unittest; same starting source and test in each profile.
method.session_cwd: Both profiles called register_task_env_overrides with cwd_source=session before the conversation. Effective Docker workspace mounted at /workspace; network disabled.
method.rootless_image: Rootless Docker; pinned source image Config and RootFS layers were compared to local rootless image before use; rootless run used matching image ID and --network=none.
method.independent_verification: After model conversation, run python -B -m unittest -v inside a new rootless network-none container; inspect git diff --check, changed paths and worktree status.

limitations: Two repeats per stack only; synthetic one-function bug and one local model. No owner preference.
Direct AIAgent probe, not Open WebUI or full gateway/UI path. Requested context is recorded; effective loaded context was not captured in this run.

The PLAIN profile returned repeated empty-workspace claims despite fixture mounts; one run hallucinated a different geometry defect and claimed the test passed when independent verification failed. This is observed output, not a proven general Hermes defect; investigate tool arguments/results and effective container mounts.
One HADES run did not complete the fix; the other corrected only geometry.py and passed. The sample does not qualify the action workflow as reliable.
HADES median two-turn AIAgent time was 37.18s, above the 30s composed-task target; TTFT is not separately measured here.
A successful HADES run left an untracked __pycache__ directory after model-run tests, while the tracked diff was only geometry.py.
Temporary image-identity wrapper compared Config+RootFS against the pinned host image and routed containers to the rootless local image ID. No production daemon/configuration used.
analysis: HADES read-only diagnosis calls exposed only read_file/search_files (2 schemas, 3,433 bytes); no patch/write_file/terminal schema or tool call appeared in either diagnostic phase. This held in both repeats.

On the explicit “Fix it.” follow-up, HADES exposed its five bounded workspace tools (9,346 bytes). One of two HADES repeats patched only geometry.py and passed the independent unittest; the other asked for more files and left the failing fixture unchanged.

PLAIN exposed eight schemas (12,590 bytes), including dynamic tool-search wrappers, in both phases. Both PLAIN repeats failed independent verification; one made 24 provider generations in its two-turn conversation and returned an unrelated triangle-area diagnosis. The PLAIN tool output described an empty workspace even though the external rootless verifier mounted and saw the fixture.

The HADES no-write diagnosis boundary is an improvement over an earlier exploratory run where the model patched during the “Why?” turn. But action reliability remains mixed, HADES latency misses the composed-task target, and PLAIN setup/tool behavior needs investigation. No preference conclusion.
